title: Connections
sub: Banks, cards and wallets that sync by themselves.
help: Choose the banks and cards you use. Only the ones you add are shown and synced.
twoLogins: Have two logins at one company (two Wise accounts, two sets of cards)? Add it again and give each a nickname. To disconnect one, press Remove on its own card.
note1: Logins are encrypted and never shown again
note3: Two failed logins pause a source
missing: Something missing? Import a CSV export from your bank or card instead (Settings → Import and export).
otpNote: A bank may ask for a one-time code. If it does, use Verify this device, or import a file (Settings → Import and export). Wise: create a personal token with read-only permissions.
nickReq: Nickname (required, so you can tell the logins apart)
histD: Reads further back than the routine sync, once. It asks for the period you pick and keeps whatever the bank still has. Nothing already in the app is duplicated.
h1825: Up to 5 years (whatever the bank has)
shotTip: Shows what the bank page looked like when the last login stopped.

hint.none: Enter the login below to get started.
hint.untested: Saved. Press Test connection to check the login.
hint.tested: The login works ({when}). Press Sync now to import your data.
hint.stale: Last synced {when}, over 2 days ago. Press Sync now.
hint.locked: Paused after two failed attempts in a row. Check the login, then press Unlock.

err.noAnswer: The bank gave no answer to the login request, so the app could not log in. This is usually the bank’s bot protection blocking the app’s browser, or a short block after several tries. Wait an hour, then press Test connection once. Press “See where it stopped” to see what the app’s browser saw. Until then, use the CSV export (Settings → Import and export).
err.noData: The bank accepted the login but sent back no data. Usually the bank wants something first: a code, a new-device check, a new password, or a notice. Or it blocks automatic access. Log in on the bank's website yourself to see what it asks for. If it asks nothing, press “See where it stopped” on the connection to see what the app’s browser saw. Until then, use the CSV export (Settings → Import and export).
err.otp: The bank asked for a one-time code by SMS, so automatic sync is paused. Press Verify this device once. Log in in the live window, enter the code, and tick “remember this device”. Banks usually only ask on a device they do not know. (Or use a CSV export: Settings → Import and export.)

job.wait: Wait for the current one to finish
job.tailOne: · usually a few minutes; a long history can take much longer. It keeps going while the bank is answering, please wait
job.tailMany: · this can take a few minutes, please wait
job.mine: {what} {src}… {time}. Please wait, do not close this page.
job.busy: {src} is busy ({what}). Wait for it to finish before starting another.

toast.opening: Opening the bank's page… this takes a few seconds

shotD: This is what the app's bank browser saw when the last login failed. A captcha, a notice or a blank page here tells us why. Every picture taken during each failed login is saved in the app's data folder, in profiles → _failed-logins (one folder per attempt, the newest 15 per bank are kept).
shotNone: No screenshot yet. Press Test connection once and let it fail, then open this again.
testLockedD: Two failures in a row. Check the credentials, then unlock it.

assist.title: Verify this device
assist.d1: This is the app’s own browser, shown live. Log in as you normally do, enter the code the bank sends you, and tick “remember this device” if it asks. When you reach your account, press
assist.d1c: . The bank then knows this browser, so automatic syncs should not ask for a code again. Only you can see this window.
assist.ph: Type here and press Send (for the code)
assist.hint: Click or tap the picture to focus a field, then type. "Type my…" fills a saved login without ever sending it to this page.
